about: What NPCs drop when they die, as the OSRS Wiki lists it (read 2026-10-28): every always item, one roll on the main table (a line's weight out of the slots, as in 3/128), then each tertiary drop on its own. The world counts as a members world, so members-only lines are in and the free-to-play-only ones (Coins x10 23/128, Nothing 30/128) are out. Items are ids with their cache names beside them; the loader warns when a name doesn't match. Clue scrolls drop as plain items until clues are their own piece.

herbs.source: OSRS Wiki, Herb drop table: the Man page's 1/22.3 for guam is 23/128 of the table times 32/128 of this, and so on down

general_seeds.source: OSRS Wiki, Drop table#General seed drop table: its first subtable, which every roll of a monster below level 49 lands on (the subtable is picked by a roll of the monster's level times 10, and below 485 that is the first); the Guard page's 1/19 potato seed is 18/128 of the guard table times 368/1008 of this. Higher levels' subtables wait for a monster that needs them

allotment_seeds.source: OSRS Wiki, Catablepon, Drops, read 2026-11-03: its allotment seed roll at 1/101, potato 1/202 down to watermelon and snape grass 1/12,928 each, so 64/128 of the roll down to 1/128. Ranged counts are taken as evenly likely (guessed)

gems.source: OSRS Wiki, Gem drop table, read 2026-11-01: each row's x/128. The chaos and nature talismans share one 3/128 row, picked by where the player is (the Wiki: typically nature above ground, chaos underground); every monster on this table so far is in the Draynor Sewers, so the row is the chaos talisman. Monsters above ground take gems_surface, the same table with the nature talisman. The last 1 is the mega-rare drop table, which isn't built: it gives nothing for now
